title: Review: Photons and the photoelectric effect; Energy levels and spectra; Ultrasound imaging; Impulse and force–time graphs; Angular measures and uniform circular motion
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: X-ULTRASOUND-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; Q02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; Q01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; D10-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C01-1#N.4a, D10-1#N.12, Q01-1#N.4b, Q02-1#N.6a, C01-1#N.12a, D10-1#N.4a, Q01-1#N.9a, Q02-1#N.13a, Q01-1#N.13. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ultrasound
items.clue: Longitudinal wave with frequency above 20 kHz, beyond human hearing.

items.label: Ground state
items.clue: Lowest allowed level of an electron in an atom, n = 1; at –13.6 eV in hydrogen.

items.label: Planck constant
items.clue: Symbol h: the energy of one quantum of light divided by its f; 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

items.label: Impulse
items.clue: Vector in N s pointing along the resultant force, not necessarily along the motion.

questions.stem: A bicycle wheel of diameter 0.700 m rotates at a steady rate about a fixed axle, making one complete revolution every 0.250 s. What is the linear speed of a point on the rim of the wheel?

Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed

questions.stem: Light with a wavelength of 500 nm in air passes from the air into water (n = 1.33). What is the energy of each photon while it travels through the water? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the speed of light in air as c.
An atom has only four energy levels: −1.50 eV, −2.50 eV, −4.00 eV and −6.00 eV. What is the energy of the emitted photon that has the SHORTEST wavelength?
questions.explanation: Largest gap: −1.50 eV → −6.00 eV, ΔE = 4.50 eV. Largest ΔE → highest f → shortest λ.

questions.stem: The drum of a washing machine has a diameter of 0.50 m. It rotates about a horizontal axis at constant speed, with a time period of 0.050 s. What is the centripetal acceleration of a sock pressed against the inside of the drum?

A sledge on level snow is pulled horizontally with a constant force of 60.0 N for 4.00 s. Throughout this time it slides forwards and the frictional force on it is 22.0 N. What is the magnitude of the impulse delivered to the sledge by the resultant force during the 4.00 s?
questions.explanation: Resultant force = 60.0 − 22.0 = 38.0 N. J = FΔt = 38.0 × 4.00 = 152 N s, forwards.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which observation from photoelectric experiments cannot be explained by the classical wave theory of light?

options.text: Photoelectrons are emitted without any measurable delay, even in very dim light.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the light is made much more intense.
More photoelectrons are emitted each second when the frequency of the light is raised.
Every photoelectron leaves the metal with kinetic energy exactly hf minus the work function.

questions.stem: An atom has energy levels at −10.0 eV (the ground state), −5.0 eV and −3.0 eV. An atom in its ground state is struck by a photon of energy 3.0 eV. What happens?

options.text: The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to the −3.0 eV energy level.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 15.0 or 13.0 eV.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 5.0 or 7.0 eV.
The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to an energy of −7.0 eV.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity
